findings.claim: Drift section absent from scripts/generate-scorecard-report.py — AC (i) and plan-doc §5 both explicitly require it.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE AC (i): 'Markdown shape: header + per-adopter table + drift section (versus prior report if available) + footer.' Plan-doc §5: 'Drift section: deltas vs prior index (verdict flips, version drift).' The implementation's render() function outputs header (lines 97–116) + adopters table (lines 128–146) + a 'Verification failures + unreachable + no-emit' detail section (lines 148–160) + footer (lines 162–170). No logic reads a prior report file from docs/scorecards/ and no drift delta is computed or emitted.
findings.impact: Operator/auditor review of aggregator PRs loses the primary change-tracking signal — which adopters flipped verdict, which bumped SCP version, which transitioned from unreachable to verified. Without drift the markdown is a snapshot with no week-over-week accountability; the plan-doc named drift as the observability rationale for this surface.
findings.mitigation: Option A (preferred): implement drift section by reading the most recent prior markdown (sorted by filename date) or comparing the current vs prior index.json, then emitting a '## Drift vs prior run' section. Option B (acceptable deferral): file as TF-023D-003 with explicit note that drift section is deferred to 023E where real adopter data first makes drift observable; annotate AC (i) in DISPATCH-NOTE as an accepted-gap per TF-023D-003. Option B requires adding TF-023D-003 to both DISPATCH-NOTE §forward-looking and STATUS.md.

findings.claim: TF-023C-007 (adopter wrapper filename must be `policy-check.yml`) is not explicitly documented in ADOPT-001 §12.7.15.
findings.evidence: STATUS.md TF-023C-007 (line 210): 'Adopter wrapper filename constraint (must be `policy-check.yml`) — document at slice 023D ADOPT-001 §13 onboarding.' ADOPT-001 §12.7.15 shows a YAML snippet with `uses: jrnb2024/standards-control-plane-/.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@<sha>` and the job named `policy-check`, but no prose sentence states that the adopter's wrapper workflow file MUST be named `policy-check.yml` or explains that the aggregator filters artifact downloads by this specific workflow filename.
findings.impact: An adopter whose existing CI wrapper is named `ci.yml`, `scp-check.yml`, or any name other than `policy-check.yml` will successfully add `scorecard-emit: true` and PR the registry entry, then experience silent failure: the aggregator's `gh run download` will find no artifact and the adopter row will appear as `no_emit`. The constraint is discoverable by reading the aggregator source but not from the onboarding doc.
findings.mitigation: Add a prose note to ADOPT-001 §12.7.15 step 2: 'Note: your wrapper workflow file must be named `policy-check.yml` — the aggregator discovers emit artifacts by searching for completed runs of this specific workflow filename. If your existing wrapper has a different filename, rename it or create a thin delegating wrapper.' Mark TF-023C-007 as closed in STATUS.md once this prose is added.

placement_argument.conclusion: CORRECT — §12.7.15 is the right structural home for the scorecard opt-in onboarding content.
placement_argument.argument: ADOPT-001 §12.7 is titled 'Federation primitive — adopter integration' and contains subsections §12.7.1 through §12.7.14, each covering a specific technical integration topic (workflow wiring, CODEOWNERS, pre-commit hook, rule-config, versioning, rule-RFC, SCP-R-004 guidance, etc.). §12.7.15 as 'Cross-repo scorecard opt-in' is a natural extension of this chain: the scorecard opt-in IS a federation primitive adopter integration concern — it extends the existing policy-check.yml@<sha> wrapper with scorecard-emit: true, using the same wrapper infrastructure §12.7.1–§12.7.4 describe. §13 is 'Recommended Adoption Phases', covering timeline and sequencing guidance for onboarding, not deep technical how-to. Placing scorecard opt-in in §13 would break §12.7 self-consistency. The plan-doc §6 row 4 reference to 'ADOPT-001 §13 onboarding section' was a draft approximation that did not anticipate the §12.7 subsection depth reached by 023D (§12.7.14 was the last section before this slice). The D-043 commit placing content at §12.7.15 was correct; the plan-doc §6 row is a non-normative prose pointer to the ADOPT-001 onboarding appendix generally, not a binding section-number constraint. No structural change is required.
